sections.heading: Project load and calculate upgrade costs
paragraphs: We interpolate between LBNL's 192 TWh in 2024 and 464 TWh in 2028 to get 298.476 TWh in 2026, then reach 649 TWh in 2030. Growth after 2030 is our assumption. New covered MW = (annual TWh - 298.476) x 1,000,000 / (8,760 x 0.80) x 0.75. Each year's added MW costs $650,000/MW, rising 1% annually from 2026. [2, 3] The faster case uses 649 x EIA server-use[y]/server-use[2030], then extends the 2049-2050 growth rate through 2056. [6]

Annual capital recovery = capital x 0.05 / (1 - 1.05^(-40)). Add 1.5% of capital for operations and maintenance. In the baseline, data centers already pay 35% of capital recovery directly, but no operating costs directly. Existing load and network cost K grow 1% a year. Half of covered growth is assigned to PJM billing areas; the rest goes to the remaining U.S. system. These are model assumptions. [3, 4, 7-15]

sections.heading: Calculate who pays
paragraphs: For each region/year: K = annual existing-network cost; C = annual assigned-upgrade cost; D = annual equivalent of existing direct upgrade funding; s = new data centers' share of billing demand. The baseline collects D directly and shares the remaining costs. AND collects C directly and removes it from shared rates, leaving K. [1, 3]
equations: Baseline = D + s(K + C - D). AND = C + sK. Extra payments = (1-s)(C-D).
Above higher-of = AND - max(baseline, C). Add results across regions and years 2030-2056.

sections.heading: Check the totals and compare with the ITC
paragraphs: In $bn: AND 232.975 - baseline 176.955 = 56.020 extra. AND - higher-of 177.396 = 55.579 above that benchmark. JCT's annual costs for 2022-2031 are 0, 0, 0, .788, 1.213, 1.213, 1.213, 2.001, 2.426, 2.425. Our 30-year ITC comparison = 3 x sum(cost[y] / 1.025^(y-2026)) = $31.674bn; 56.020 / 31.674 = 1.77. The extension is our calculation, not a JCT score; the ratio compares dollar amounts, not equivalent benefits. [3, 5]
